story.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia Arrives in Spain After Leaving the U.S.
story.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, an El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported by ICE last year, has left the United States and arrived in Spain. His departure marks the conclusion of a 20-month legal battle related to his deportation, which became emblematic of the Trump administration's immigration policies. Garcia traveled to Spain with his wife, stating he feels like a 'free man' after the ordeal.

explore_lenses.label: Why does leaving end the civil case?
explore_lenses.title: The court case is closed, not a ruling on every dispute
explore_lenses.summary: His departure removed the immediate basis for the Maryland civil case over his detention and removal, so the judge closed it as moot. That procedural ending does not itself resolve the broader legal and policy disputes raised by his deportation.

claims.text: On November 25, 2026, U.S. District Judge Paula Xinis dissolved the injunctions, denied remaining motions as moot, and closed Abrego Garcia's civil case after receiving confirmation that he had departed the United States.

Before his departure, Judge Xinis ordered the government to permit unimpeded travel, remove his ankle monitor before boarding, and avoid actions that could prevent him from leaving; the departure therefore occurred under court-supervised conditions rather than through a completed third-country removal attempt.

The Supreme Court's April 2025 order had said the government must facilitate his release from Salvadoran custody and handle his case as if he had not been improperly sent to El Salvador, making the case a prominent test of judicial remedies for an erroneous removal.

explore_lenses.label: What legal matters remain unresolved?
explore_lenses.title: The criminal appeal continues despite his departure
explore_lenses.summary: The departure closes the civil removal litigation, but not the government's appeal of the dismissal of federal human-smuggling charges. The appellate court could leave the dismissal in place or reinstate the indictment.

claims.text: A federal judge dismissed the human-smuggling case in May 2026 on vindictive-prosecution grounds; the Justice Department appealed, and CBS reported Sixth Circuit arguments were scheduled for February.

The Justice Department argues that career prosecutors brought the indictment based on evidence and law rather than retaliation, and asks the Sixth Circuit to reverse the dismissal and reinstate the case.
Forecast: If the Sixth Circuit accepts the Justice Department's arguments, it could reinstate the indictment; if it rejects them, the dismissal would remain in force unless further review is pursued.

story_report.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who was mistakenly deported by ICE last year, left the United States for Spain on Nov. 22, 2026, and arrived there with his wife. The move ended his 20-month legal battle over the deportation. After receiving confirmation that he had left the country, U.S. District Judge Paula Xinis dissolved injunctions, denied remaining motions as moot and closed his civil case on Nov. 25, ending the active civil proceedings without resolving the legality of earlier government conduct.

sections.heading: Abrego Garcia’s Court-Supervised Departure
sections.body: Before Abrego Garcia left, Judge Xinis ordered the government to allow his unimpeded travel, remove his ankle monitor before he boarded and refrain from actions that could prevent his departure. The conditions meant he left under court supervision rather than through a completed attempt to remove him to a third country. The Supreme Court had ordered in April 2025 that the government facilitate his release from Salvadoran custody and handle his case as though he had not been improperly sent to El Salvador.

sections.heading: Abrego Garcia’s Pending Criminal Appeal
sections.body: A separate human-smuggling case against Abrego Garcia was dismissed by a federal judge in May 2026 on vindictive-prosecution grounds. The Justice Department appealed and has argued that career prosecutors brought the indictment based on evidence and law, not retaliation; it is seeking reinstatement of the case. CBS reported that Sixth Circuit arguments were scheduled for February.

unresolved.text: Closing the civil case as moot does not determine whether the government’s earlier conduct was lawful or settle policy disputes over comparable removals.
The outcome and timing of the Sixth Circuit appeal remain unresolved, and the available record does not show whether Abrego Garcia’s move to Spain will affect future criminal-court procedures.

related_stories.title: Thousands Protest in Athens Over Rising Living Costs
related_stories.summary: On November 25, 2026, approximately 14,000 people marched in Athens as part of a 24-hour strike against rising living costs and stagnant wages. The industrial action led to significant disruptions, including halted metro services, grounded flights, and ferries remaining in port.

related_stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Seven in Ukraine; Kyiv Targets Refineries
related_stories.summary: Russian drone attacks resulted in the deaths of seven people across six Ukrainian regions, targeting infrastructure including a gas production facility and a thermal power plant. In response, Ukraine launched drone strikes on Russian oil refineries in the Samara and Rostov regions, as well as an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod, leading to at least one reported death in the Samara region.
